summary: Restored 1943 L-4 groundhouse in the Rogue River National Forest, formerly Squaw Peak Lookout, now a seasonal recreation rental.

facts.status_note: Restored; open to visitors and rentable.

access.note: Gated combination-lock access road, steep and winding; combination provided with reservation.

visit.trail_note: Access road may not suit passenger vehicles or large trucks; firepit on site, no firewood provided.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Rogue River National Forest / Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest)

events.note: NHLR and firelookout.com date construction to 1943; Recreation.gov instead gives 1942.
Last year staffed full-time; afterward used for emergencies and early-season coverage of Dutchman Peak.

Listed as Squaw Peak Lookout under the US Forest Service Historic Structures on the Rogue River National Forest multiple listing; the NPGallery asset record gives a Date Published of 12/29/2000 (no separate listing date field rendered), so the year is corrected from the earlier placeholder of 2003.
Renamed from Squaw Peak Lookout to Acorn Woman Peak Lookout approximately five years before a September 2026 NHLR site update.
NHLR description states the lookout has been restored and is open to visitors.

evidence.supports: L-4 groundhouse, built 1943, restored and open, renamed ~5 years before 9-22-26 update
evidence.quote: Squaw Peak Lookout is a classic new model L-4 groundhouse with catwalk. Build in 1943, it has been restored and is open to visitors. 9-22-26 The tower name has been updated from Squaw Peak Lookout to Acorn Woman Peak Lookout. It was renamed approx 5 yrs ago.

evidence.supports: Built 1942 per Recreation.gov, glass-walled, rental during snow-free season, 5-night max, gated combination lock, steep access road, rattlesnakes/ticks/poison oak
evidence.quote: Acorn Woman Peak Lookout was constructed in 1942. It is an L-4 style cabin... Access road is steep and windy and may not be suitable for passenger vehicles or large trucks. Access road is gated and locked with combination lock.

evidence.supports: Used ahead of snowmelt on Dutchman Peak, last staffed full-time 1966
evidence.quote: This L-4 cab, built in 1943, was last staffed fulltime in 1966. It was then used for emergencies and in early season when access to Dutchman's Peak was blocked by snow.

evidence.supports: NRHP listing as Squaw Peak Lookout under Rogue River National Forest multiple listing
evidence.quote: Multiple Listing: US Forest Service Historic Structures on the Rogue River National Forest MPS

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com both give 1943; Recreation.gov gives 1942. Kept both and noted the discrepancy rather than picking one.

sources.title: Acorn Woman Peak Lookout campground listing

notes_for_editor: Built-year conflict (1942 vs 1943) unresolved; story notes both. Fact-check 2026-10-04: re-fetched the NPGallery asset record directly; it has no explicit 'listing date' field, but gives Date Published 12/29/2000, so the nrhp_listed event year was corrected from a placeholder 2003 to 2000. The story itself states no year for the NRHP listing, so no story edit was needed there. All four footnoted citations and their quoted evidence were spot-checked against the live sources and confirmed verbatim.
